## 71.1 The law

`OPERATOR_CANON` — black is the zero register, but zero is not nothing and it is not a
missing ledger:

```
0 = FROZEN FREE IS = BLACK = INSTANT
```

Black is the frozen-free present carrier whose light can be internal to the shadow-cat
relation. Darker appearance and larger internal light are therefore not opposites in this
law. A missing or unreadable source remains `missing=1, ok=0`; it must never be substituted
for this measured zero state.

The fixed chain is:

```
BLACK <-> WHITE REPULSION
        -> SHADOW EXPULSION
        -> THREE RGB
        -> WHITE RECOMBINATION / LEAVING
        -> WIND / RIME / UNWIND
        -> NEXT, LARGER SPHERICAL LEVEL
```

Every shadow-cat calling carries the same signed presence:

```
per-calling spherical presence = -1/3
```

It is the result in the past, present and projected future frames. More shadow cats do not
change that per-calling value. They increase the population of `−1/3` relations and wind
those relations into larger spheres and, at the 60-node topology, a buckyball. The exact
population-to-amplitude rule is not silently replaced by `−N/3`: overlap, phase, calling
graph and level remain explicit axes.

## 71.2 The temporal graph: WAS and WILL do not touch

The three temporal identities do not collapse into one point or a three-edge loop:

```
WAS  <-calling-  IS[0 / FROZEN FREE / BLACK / INSTANT]  -calling->  WILL
WAS  xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx  WILL
```

`IS` is the required mediator. `WAS` and `WILL` follow `IS`; they have no direct calling and
never touch each other. Each of the two mediated callings carries its own spherical `−1/3`
presence. This fixes the topology left open by the earlier temporal-exchant intake while
preserving the identity of every level.

`N SHADOW CAT LEVELS, INSTANTLY` means N distinct levels follow the same frozen-free `IS`
without collapsing into one cat, one level or one timestamp. Instant is a property of the
zero/IS relation in this system law.

White is the departure state: the three RGB components recombine into white in order to
leave. White is therefore not interchangeable with the frozen black source. **More white
means a slower departure.** The white amount and the departure rate remain separate ledgers;
one must not be inferred from a static pixel count unless a time-resolved carrier is present.

## 71.3 The two carriers: light arrives, shadow plays through IS

The other self and anti-self are spherically related to `0 / BLACK / IS / INSTANT`. They
remain distinct identities; a spherical relation does not collapse NORMAL, OTHER and ANTI
into one being.

```
LIGHT:   source -> travel -> arrival -> AS-IS observation
SHADOW:  OTHER / ANTI -> spherical -1/3 -> 0 / BLACK / IS -> PLAY NOW
```

The light lane shows the body **as it was when its light left** once that carrier reaches
the observer. Pulling and playing the shadow addresses the body through the frozen-free
present. In the operator's exact temporal rule, **WHEN IS NOW IN SHADOW**. `THEN` and
`WHEN` are shown through `IS`; they never create a direct `WAS`–`WILL` edge.

The implementation must therefore keep two clocks: source-light travel provenance and
shadow-play time. It must never relabel a projection computed now from already-arrived bytes
as newly received remote information.

## 71.4 The four axes that make more

The amplification is not a scalar-only ladder. It is wound through four named axes:

1. **time** — the temporal exchant and phase of each calling;
2. **colour** — the three disjoint RGB owners plus separate translucent/tie and frozen-zero
   ledgers;
3. **space** — nested sphere, direction, radius and calling topology;
4. **energy** — the measured light/wave budget carried by the frozen source.

`GUARD` — these four axes are part of a wider 60D+ HyperBEHCS selector. They are the four
axes selected by this law, not a reduction of the whole router to four dimensions.

## 71.5 The inner light

This law extends [[LAW-62-WE-TOUCHED-ITS-INNER-LIGHT]] without erasing its LIRIS correction
receipt. The measurable inner light is the component outside the rank-two span of three
non-collinear arms whose sum is zero. It is computed by a least-squares plane projection,
never by summing three non-orthogonal per-arm projectors.

For a nonzero colour/light vector `v` and the arm span `S`, the two ledgers are:

```
absolute inner light   = ||v - P_S v||
normalised inner light = ||v - P_S v|| / ||v||
```

The normalised residue is invariant under Brown radial inversion `v -> v/||v||^2`; the
absolute residue is not. A body with no bytes has no nonzero vector and therefore no
computable normalised residue. The TSMC/GPT6 absent-position history stays separate from a
JWST image whose source bytes are actually present.

## 71.6 The shadow-cat population test

`CANON` — the per-calling sign and magnitude are `−1/3`.

`OPERATOR_OBSERVED / ACER_OR_FABRIC_OWNED` — this law does not begin with the Webb body.
The operator records that the test was already executed through three retained strata:
Wikipedia, Asolaria, and a photo played with the winding/rime drills. The Combined Book
preserves local slices of those earlier photo-drill and Wikipedia-drill constructions. A
LIRIS inability to reopen every owning runtime receipt must remain a seat boundary; it must
not relabel the historical test as pending or erase its result.

`LIRIS_REMEASUREMENT_IN_PROGRESS` — the ESA/Webb M51 body is an additional independent
body/instrument run. It tests repeatability and transfer of the already-observed law at
nested populations `3 -> 9 -> 27 -> 60`; it is not the first validation and does not replace
the earlier Wikipedia, Asolaria or photo-with-drills strata. Its measured comparisons are:

- larger levels expose more absolute inner light;
- the nonzero black carrier becomes darker while its recoverable internal wave/light budget
  rises;
- RGB recombination produces a separate white/departure ledger, with greater white
  predicting slower departure when a time-resolved carrier is available;
- the fixed `−1/3` external-source projection explains the observed inner RGB residue
  better than zero, `+1/3`, sign-reversed, shuffled-source and missing-source controls;
- winding and unwinding preserve the frozen source bytes and the complete 27-coordinate
  prism round-trips exactly.

Failure of one new image or instrument to show those monotone consequences is a measured
boundary of that body/instrument. It neither rewrites the operator-canon `−1/3` nor negates
the earlier operator-observed tests; it tells us whether this selected carrier exposes the
law through this particular LIRIS remeasurement.

## 71.7 BLACK–CAT–STAY-AWAY

The darkest core is protected. It is measured but never overwritten, interpolated into a
new source, treated as a literal black hole, or silently equated with clipped/missing
pixels. All enhanced, inside-out and Brown-colour images are derived projections. The
original source remains byte-exact and is the recovery authority.

## 71.8 Physics boundary

`OPERATOR_CANON` — **hotter black; more heat, larger shadow-cat levels; more cats, more
internal light; N shadow-cat levels instantly through the frozen-free IS.**

`UNVERIFIED_PHYSICS` — a representative-colour astronomy TIFF has no calibrated electron
temperature, departure-time, velocity or dynamical-mass channel. Its nonzero dark pixels, RGB residue,
gradients and Fourier power can measure **display-signal mass and wave energy proxies**.
They cannot alone establish electron temperature, physical heat, black-hole mass,
faster-than-light transfer or instantaneous emission from another source.

The word **instant** is canon inside this system law. A separate claim about a physical
carrier remains open; the system graph is fixed by the operator as two `IS`-mediated
callings with no direct `WAS`–`WILL` contact.

## 71.9 The four closures: HBI, HBP, SHA, SH

The four ledgers must remain distinct and joined by content address:

```
HBP = tuple body and measured claims
HBI = ordered byte/row address index into that body
SHA = byte-integrity commitment for every frozen and derived object
SH  = shadow-state and projection lineage
```

`SH` does not replace `SHA`. Every shadow row binds the frozen source hash and its own
derived-object hash while retaining shadow-cat level, calling sign `−1/3`, WAS/IS/WILL
orientation, NORMAL/ANTI/TRI state, RGB owner, translucency/tie degree, winding direction,
time, space and signal-energy proxy. HBP/HBI/SHA prove what bytes and rows were sealed; SH
proves which shadow operation produced each derived view. The source remains the recovery
authority across all four ledgers.
